reviewMode: Independent read-only review of world profile migration, main-character identity, local portrait/dialogue UI, phone edit/save RPC, and consented introduction generation. Production files were not modified.
finalBuildBindingStatus: Final production bundle and all three built/delivered/installed PNG scripts independently verified byte-for-byte after installation.

resolvedFindings.finding: Legacy world contacts permit summaries up to 2,000 characters. Passing the complete value as the new phone summary field violated the phone contract limit of 500, which rejected bind/sync for otherwise valid legacy saves.
resolvedFindings.resolution: contactsOf now bounds only the phone summary field to 500; the full description and authoritative world summary remain unchanged. New user edits retain the 500-character constraint.
resolvedFindings.verification: Source correction independently read. Parent owns the added regression test and full build.

conclusion: No unresolved substantive blocking defect was identified after the legacy-summary correction in the reviewed scope. This is not a claim of native-client or real-model execution.
checked: Schema 1.11.0 reconstructs supported old versions without resettling gameplay; legacy contact IDs, names, summaries, affinities, phone references and story text remain intact, with deterministic profile defaults.
Encounter identity derives from the saved scene seed and anchor. Confirmation reuses the source person ID; rename changes profile data without replacing NPC identity or phone event/read IDs.

Profile edits use a parsed clone and write the authoritative chat before publishing model state. Phone mirror creation follows a successful callback; failed mirror writes cache the already committed profile for same-request retries.

A profile save does not advance the game clock, spend resources or run story actions. Introduction generation returns editable text without adding contacts, story, messages or gameplay state; only a later explicit save commits it.

Generation is initiated by the explicitly labeled consent button. It uses a dedicated protocol with target evidence, up to six related turns and 2,400 total related-turn characters, and rejects actions/events/messages in the result.

The introduction prompt contains target evidence rather than the ordinary full action catalog; trusted portrait thumbnails are produced locally, used by the phone UI and are not passed to the introduction prompt.

Epoch, chat session, phone sequence and open-panel checks discard late generated introductions after phone close or session change. The phone form also checks draft identity and view disposal before applying a late result.
Phone requests validate their session and stable IDs; old-chat leases cannot save/generate through a replacement binding. Ordinary phone contact settings are not used for major-character saves.

Expandable dialogue stays in the existing story reader with framework-escaped text. Explicit encounters select a deterministic portrait immediately; confirmed profiles override the same identity rather than allocating new artwork randomly.

additionalCheck.kind: One bounded in-memory concurrency probe, no production or phone storage writes.
additionalCheck.implementation: Loaded the current story-phone adapter with mocked artwork/environment dependencies and the real phone story-host. A delayed sync was followed by a queued profile save and another queued sync.
additionalCheck.result: The normal adapter queue did not reproduce the initially suspected stale-profile overwrite; both final world and phone profile names were New. This concern is not listed as a defect.

limitations: No complete unit, browser or Python suite was rerun by this reviewer; parent execution evidence is recorded separately.
No real model request, original installed native SillyTavern page validation or physical TauriTavern validation was performed.
Separately installed legacy phone-extension synchronization is outside this PNG audit; the packaged embedded phone is covered through exact bundle equality.
